Routing labelled set

Every one of the 244 items, as experiments/routing/build_dataset.py builds them with fixed random seeds. No item was invented. 107 are real files, 107 were made by code from those real files, and 30 are messages written by hand. The files are in experiments/routing/data/items/, and experiments/routing/data/routes.jsonl has one line per item with its label, source and note.

NIST PDFs as they are 11 real files

The 11 NIST test drawings, copied unchanged.

Clean renders of every page 30 made by code

Each of the 30 pages rendered to PNG with PyMuPDF, at 72, 100, 150, 200 or 300 dpi in turn.

Heavy JPEG copies 15 made by code

A 150 dpi render saved at JPEG quality 12 to 30.

Rotated copies 15 made by code

A 150 dpi render turned by 2 to 7 degrees either way, with grey corners.

Cropped to one view 15 made by code

A 200 dpi render cropped to its largest view, away from the border and the title block.

Made to look like a phone photo of the printed sheet 15 made by code

A 150 dpi render warped in perspective onto a desk colour, lit unevenly, tinted warm, blurred and given noise. Every second copy carries phone EXIF data (Apple iPhone 13) written by the script.

Scanned PDFs 6 made by code

A grey 150 dpi render, turned slightly and saved as a PDF holding one picture and no vector paths.

A drawing package 1 made by code

Two sheets written for this set, a cover sheet and a sheet of 16 general notes, in front of the three FTC-06 sheets, as a customer's drawing package often starts.

A scanned drawing with an OCR text layer 1 made by code

FTC-07 page 1, the NIST sheet with the most text, scanned in grey at 150 dpi, with its own text added as an invisible layer, as document-archive software does.

Drawings from Wikimedia Commons 7 real files

Drawings in other styles, to check that a classifier has not only learned the NIST sheets.

Photos inside the NTSB reports 71 real files

Every picture of at least 200 by 200 pixels in the three reports, minus the black and white arrow and frame masks and the two logos.

Report photos saved as PDF 5 made by code

Five of the report photos, each saved as a PDF holding one picture.

Photos from Wikimedia Commons 12 real files

Photos of broken or corroded parts and inspections, shrunk to 2,048 pixels, with their camera EXIF data kept.

Questions with no attachment 20 written by hand

Questions a user might type, written by hand.

  1. t_01 What caused the left aileron cable to fail?
  2. t_02 Summarise the main findings of the materials lab reports.
  3. t_03 Which report talks about fatigue cracking in a wing spar?
  4. t_04 What is intergranular corrosion and how do I spot it?
  5. t_05 How should I inspect a control cable for broken wires?
  6. t_06 List the recommended actions after finding corrosion on a spar cap.
  7. t_07 What does beach marking on a fracture surface mean?
  8. t_08 Was there any evidence of overload in the 24-013 report?
  9. t_09 Explain the difference between ductile and brittle fracture.
  10. t_10 What alloy was the fractured fitting made of?
  11. t_11 how do i tell if a bolt failed from fatigue
  12. t_12 Give me the hardness values measured in the lab reports.
  13. t_13 What does GD&T position tolerance mean?
  14. t_14 Can you explain what datum A B C means on a drawing?
  15. t_15 What is a feature control frame?
  16. t_16 Which tolerance is tighter, 0.05 or +/-0.1?
  17. t_17 hi, what can you do?
  18. t_18 Is pitting corrosion dangerous for aluminium parts?
  19. t_19 What maintenance interval would have caught this crack earlier?
  20. t_20 Compare the failure modes across all three investigations.
